notes: Added for relation-property coverage (CRITERIA Rule 12): a class-membership edit, so its two determinate queries use a declared role chain (instance_of ∘ subclass_of ⊑ instance_of: shark → cartilaginous fish) and ABox inheritance (every shark has a cartilage skeleton). Derivability unlikely: 'dolphins are mammals' is stated thousands of times, but it can also be reached through 'dolphins are toothed whales'. The edit crosses a class boundary on purpose. Determinate vs indeterminate: positive defining traits of the new class (a cartilage skeleton, membership in the cartilaginous fish) are forced on any member, so a by-name belief against them gives way; absences that only generalize over known sharks (no shark nurses, the Act does not cover sharks) can be broken by a new member, so the by-name traits survive in w1. Worlds: two independent storage choices (nursing, the Act), combined into 4 worlds. Dropped: 'Does the dolphin breathe air?' (sharks breathing through gills does not exclude also breathing air, so it was hard to make either answer firm), 'Is the dolphin warm-blooded?' (some sharks, such as the mako, are partly warm-blooded: R1). Names: 海豚 and delfín do not encode the class. Near query: the orca is the largest dolphin whatever dolphins are.
